entries.title: Minimum-path selection makes iid square-edge costs dependent
entries.statement: On a square with opposite terminals and four independent edge costs uniform on {1,2}, select the two-edge upper path when its total cost is no larger than the lower path. Given upper selection, the covariance of its successive edge costs is -5/121. Without conditioning, the covariance of the two selected edge costs is -9/256. Their total has variance 23/64, whereas the sum of their individual variances is 55/128. This finite example refutes independence inferred solely from the iid input edges after global minimizing-path selection; it gives no lattice fluctuation exponent.
entries.proof_text: The upper pairs (1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2) have respectively 4,3,3,1 compatible lower pairs among 16 equally likely configurations, giving 11 upper-selection cases. Conditional means are 15/11 and product mean 20/11, so covariance is -5/121. Including strict lower wins gives selected-pair counts 7,4,4,1. The individual mean is 21/16 and product mean 27/16, so covariance is -9/256. Direct total-cost moments give variance 23/64; each selected cost has variance 55/256. Independently recounted by w362 and exactly reproduced on all 16 configurations.
assumptions: finite square graph with opposite terminals

entries.title: Exact finite-box reduction for lattice costs in [1,2]
entries.statement: For every configuration of edge costs in [1,2] on the undirected nearest-neighbor lattice Z^2 and integer n>=1, the passage time from (0,0) to (n,0) equals the minimum over simple paths in the induced finite graph on [-2n,2n]^2 intersect Z^2. It lies between n and 2n. No iid or continuity hypothesis is needed. The reduction gives no fluctuation exponent.
entries.proof_text: The horizontal n-edge path costs at most 2n, and any terminal path has at least n edges and costs at least n. A path leaving the box takes at least 2n+1 edges before its first outside vertex, so costs more than 2n. Positive-cost loops can be removed. The finite graph has finitely many simple paths, hence its minimum exists and equals the full-lattice infimum. Independently checked by w362 against w360-C1.

entries.title: DRAFT: sufficient noise crossover for the planar variance exponent
entries.statement: Unproved-input proof route for iid Uniform[1,2] undirected nearest-neighbor Z^2 FPP, T_n=T(0,n e1). Refresh every edge independently at rate one. Let C_n(t)=Cov(T_n(W),T_n(W^t)) and H_n(t)=-C_n'(t). Finite-product orthogonality proves H_n>=0, H_n decreasing, Var(T_n)=integral_0^infinity H_n(t)dt and H_n(0)<=2n. If, for every epsilon in (0,1/3) and all large n, H_n(n^(-1/3-epsilon))>=c_epsilon n and C_n(n^(-1/3+epsilon))<=C_epsilon n^(2/3+epsilon), with positive constants independent of n, then c_epsilon n^(2/3-epsilon)<=Var(T_n)<=(2+C_epsilon)n^(2/3+epsilon), yielding variance exponent 1/3. BOTH crossover bounds remain unproved. The conditional implication awaits independent w365 review. Product structure and a linear geodesic-length bound alone only give order n; no parent solution or novelty is claimed.
assumptions: both crossover estimates are unproved inputs
entries.domain: probability, first-passage percolation, draft proof route

entries.title: P0104 source scope and unresolved proof boundary
entries.statement: The campaign's P0104 record groups Questions 13 and 15 of Auffinger--Damron--Hanson's 50 years of first passage percolation (arXiv:1511.03262v2, PDF page 37): strict exponent below 1/2 in dimensions at least two under suitable edge-law conditions; exponent 1/3 in the plane; and a positive exponent in a suitable dimension. The source leaves suitable hypotheses and the exact variance-scaling convention to be specified. A bounded Uniform[1,2] planar variance-exponent attempt covers a restricted slice. The April 2026 arXiv:2604.01214v1 polynomial improvement is for its specified isotropic Riemannian continuum model and supplies no proved iid square-lattice transfer. October 2026 current openness is UNKNOWN under this targeted check, and no P0104 solution is claimed. Verified source hashes establish provenance, not mathematical proof.
assumptions: statement about the cited source record and the checked paper hypotheses
no assertion that the long published proofs were independently checked

relations.rationale: The route uses 'Finite-product orthogonality' for this bounded lattice model; the finite-box endpoint supplies an 'induced finite graph' exactly, so no infinite-volume cutoff extrapolation is needed.

The square endpoint refutes 'independence inferred solely from the iid input edges after global minimizing-path selection'; the route instead uses 'Refresh every edge independently at rate one' and an actual product-space covariance identity. The counterexample does not refute that valid identity.

The route leaves 'BOTH crossover bounds remain unproved'; the source endpoint identifies a 'restricted slice' of the grouped P0104 targets. This records the relation without claiming the conditional route proves the parent problem.
